rows: Tornado developed several miles west northwest of Sonora along Ranch Road 1312. The tornado paralleled the road for about a mile before dissipating. No damage was reported.
Penny to nickel size hail was reported.
There was some wind and hail damage reported in and around Sonora.
Hail just larger than golfballs covered the road on Highway 277.
Tree limbs were blown down at the KHOS Radio Station.
Quarter size hail was reported four miles east of the intersection of the Caverns of Sonora Road and Ranch Road 189.
Golf ball size hail was reported.
A National Weather Service employee reported golf ball sized hail along Interstate 10 about 15.6 miles east of Sonora.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported golf ball size hail just south of Sonora, causing broken windows and dents on vehicles.
Public reported 4 inch diameter Live Oak tree limbs were snapped off by damaging thunderstorm winds about 5 miles east of Sonora.
Golf ball to baseball size hail damaged skylights of a residence.
A trained spotter reported numerous tree branches down by damaging thunderstorm winds.
The broadcast media shared pictures via Twitter of golf ball size hail near Sonora. The time of the event is based on radar.
A picture of quarter size to half dollar size hail was received via social media.
The public reported baseball size hail 12 miles east of Sonora.
A report from Facebook indicated golf ball size hail fell about 5 miles north of Sonora.
The public measured hail at least 2.25 inches in diameter in southern Sutton County.
Public reported golf ball size hail.
Law enforcement reported that trees and large tree limbs were blown down and shingles were blown off roofs.
A mesonet station measured a 58 mph wind gust.
Public report from social media of quarter size hail covering the ground at the rest stop west of Sonora.
NWS storm survey of wind damage to a wool warehouse. Significant wind damage to the metal roof of the warehouse. Winds were estimated at 85 mph based on the roof damage to the warehouse.
The Sutton County Sheriff's Office reported numerous roofs blown off, electrical power poles down, and numerous large trees down just south of Sonora off of U.S. HWY 277.
